subtype: Approach: collecting resources instead of studying [Pitfall]
passage: In their small house in Hisar, Nikita's phone buzzed all day. She had joined fourteen study groups for the bank exams. Every morning she forwarded the best PDFs to her own "Important" folder. By March it held 312 files. She had switched online teachers three times: one was too slow, one too fast, one had a better accent. Her younger brother Anirban watched her scroll. "Didi, which book are you on?" "I'm collecting the best material first. Then I'll study properly." Her mock test that Sunday came back at 38 out of 100. She scrolled back through her notes. Four books started, none finished. The folder of 312 PDFs sat there, most of them unopened. Anirban peeked at the score and quietly put a cup of tea beside her. She didn't forward anything for the rest of the day.

qa.q: How many files were in the Important folder by March?
How might Nikita have felt on seeing 38 out of 100?
qa.a: Nikita likely felt shaken and disheartened, seeing that all the collecting hadn't turned into learning.

qa.q: What would you change first in Nikita's approach?
qa.a: Pick one book and one teacher, finish them, and leave most of the groups, so the time goes into studying rather than collecting.

qa.q: How does Anirban respond to the score?
qa.a: Anirban notices her disappointment and quietly brings tea, showing care without adding pressure.

grounding: Shows a candidate joining many groups, downloading dozens of PDFs and switching teachers, feeling busy but never finishing one book, so little is retained.

subtype: Approach: collecting resources instead of studying [Pitfall]
passage: Paulo was preparing for the national civil service exam in Curitiba, and he was always busy. He followed nine study channels, had signed up for three online courses, and saved every summary shared in his exam forums. His laptop desktop was a wall of folders: "Law PDFs", "Law PDFs 2", "Best notes FINAL". Elif, his flatmate, a master's student from Istanbul, watched him download another bundle one evening. "Have you finished any of these?" she asked. Paulo laughed. "Not yet. I'm building my library first." Two months later, a friend quizzed him on administrative law over dinner. He knew the names of five well-known teachers and the titles of eleven books. He couldn't answer three basic questions. That night he opened "Best notes FINAL" and realised he had never read past page six.

qa.q: How many study channels did Paulo follow?
How did Paulo feel when he couldn't answer the basic questions?
qa.a: Paulo likely felt embarrassed and shaken, realising he knew about books but not what was in them.

qa.q: What else could Paulo do starting tomorrow?
qa.a: Paulo could choose one course and one book, set the rest aside, and test himself each week without notes.

qa.q: How might Elif see Paulo's library?
qa.a: Elif sees a lot of collecting and very little finishing, which is why her simple question lands.

grounding: Illustrates a candidate collecting courses, channels and PDFs and feeling busy, but never finishing any, so little is retained.
